I will keep the full 10.1 mu in my usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is what matches my land, my irrigation, and the way I have farmed for years. I am 70, so I will not chase complicated or risky methods. I will use stable seed types, moderate fertilizer, and a workload I can manage with my family. For winter wheat, I will use improved seed, give enough nitrogen to support tillering and grain filling, add phosphorus and potassium for roots and straw strength, irrigate at the key times with my well, and control diseases and weeds with two pesticide rounds. For summer maize, I will use hybrid seed because it gives me steadier output on this land, then I will keep fertilizer a bit higher than wheat, give two irrigations if rainfall is not enough, and do two pesticide applications mainly for weeds and insects. I will save labor where I can, so after wheat I will go into maize with no-tillage, while for wheat I will use rotary tillage to make a workable seedbed. I am aiming for steady yield, not the highest possible yield, because I want the crop to be reliable and the costs to stay under control.
